info.title: Starboard API
info.description: Make a key in Starboard: Settings, Security, API keys. Send it as Authorization: Bearer sb_read_... or sb_manage_... A read key reads; a manage key also does the everyday actions (each POST, marked x-right: manage). x-scope is the scope a key needs. Errors are RFC 9457 problem details. Lists use limit and cursor. Answers carry an ETag; send If-None-Match to get 304.

post.description: Only for keys that ticked Updates: a key with no scopes does not have them. One update runs at a time. Each has the same backup, health check and way back as on the pages: Starboard runs update.sh; Reelix and the other apps keep their old image until the new one is healthy; a plug-in runs its before step, moves its settings, waits for its health check and goes back by itself if it fails. Never from an address: only the version Starboard already found.

get.summary: Every download that needs attention or failed, with its details, and as Markdown for an AI helper
get.description: Each app's queue is asked once when you call this (at most every 10 seconds), never on a timer. markdown starts with a short prompt telling an AI helper what to do, then one section for each download. Keys, passwords, tokens, private addresses and full download addresses are taken out; paths are only those in media and download folders.

get.summary: How long Starboard keeps its logs, the most they may take, and what they take now
get.description: Only for keys that ticked Logs: a key with no scopes does not have them. Whichever limit comes first removes the oldest days: when a new day starts, when the limits change and when the size written passes the limit. They cover Starboard's own log (with its jobs, updates and plug-ins' lines), the API's audit log and the last Starboard update's log. apps is the apps' own limit, read from Docker.

post.summary: AI assistants: the Model Context Protocol, read-only tools about the media server
post.description: The MCP Streamable HTTP transport: send one JSON-RPC 2.0 message as JSON (no batches) and get one JSON answer, never a stream. It takes initialize, ping, tools/list and tools/call; notifications, with no id, get 202 and no body. Off until the owner activates AI assistants in Settings, Security, API keys (403 mcp_off). Only a Read only key (403 read_key_needed). tools/list gives the tools the key's scopes cover: search_library (library), recently_added, coming_up and now_playing (media), downloads_in_progress and download_problems (downloads), requests (requests), app_health (apps) and disk_space (system). Each reads the same as its /api/v1 route and changes nothing. Each tools/call is written to the audit log. An Origin header from another site is refused (403 origin_refused). MCP versions 2025-06-18 and 2025-03-26; send MCP-Protocol-Version after initialize.

200.description: The JSON-RPC answer: result, or error with a JSON-RPC code such as -32601 for a method Starboard does not take.

202.description: A notification was taken. No body.

400.description: Not JSON, or not one JSON-RPC 2.0 message (a JSON-RPC error), or an MCP version Starboard does not speak (a problem).

post.summary: A plug-in raises or clears one of its alerts, sent through Starboard's own alerts

key.description: The plug-in's own name for the alert, such as check-router. Raised once until cleared.

message.description: Sent after the plug-in's name, such as On demand: Ping: no answer for 3 checks in a row.

example.title: Router is not answering
example.message: Ping: no answer for 3 checks in a row.

sent.description: false when it was already raised, there was nothing to clear, or alerts are off in Settings, Alerts

post.description: Only the plug-in's own key, while the plug-in is active and its approved permissions include alerts:send: any other key gets 404 not_found. The one write a plug-in's read-only key may do. An alert goes out once until it is cleared, to where Starboard sends its own (ntfy, Gotify or a webhook), as the alert.raised and alert.cleared events and in the log, and only while alerts are on. Up to 30 new alerts an hour for each plug-in (429 rate_limited with Retry-After); raising one that is already raised does not count.

key.description: A Starboard API key, sb_read_... or sb_manage_...

cursor.name: cursor
cursor.description: The next_cursor of the previous answer.

idempotency.name: Idempotency-Key
idempotency.description: Send the same value again to get the first answer back without doing it twice. Kept for 24 hours.

X-Request-Id.description: Yours, or one Starboard made; also in problem.instance.

state.description: some-updated only for Install all updates (kind batch): some updated, some did not.
went-back and held only in Install all updates, where each step is one update.

big_change.description: An app or Reelix: the new version is a new major version (1.5.0).

reelix.description: true when the download is Reelix's.

kind.description: film, episode, album, book or radio episode, when known.

app_state.description: The app's own state words, such as tracked_state importBlocked.

messages.description: Every message from the app, with secrets and private addresses taken out.

download_client_ids.description: download_id (the torrent's id or the Usenet download's id) and, for Reelix, client_id_in_reelix.

paths.description: output: where it downloaded to, as the app sees it inside its container. Only media and download folders.

ids.description: The ids in the app (in Reelix, Reelix's ids): queue, and film, series, episode, album, book or radio show.

tried.description: What Starboard already did about it, oldest first.

method.description: initialize, ping, tools/list or tools/call; or a notification, such as notifications/initialized, with no id.

result.description: initialize: protocolVersion, capabilities, serverInfo and instructions. tools/list: tools. tools/call: content, structuredContent and isError.
